name: Low Voltage Directive
impact_assessment: joint impact assessment SEC(2011) 1376 for the New Legislative Framework alignment package
evidence_rating: thin: one Commission evaluation based mainly on stakeholder views; little quantitative data
summary: The Commission's 2021 evaluation found the Directive fairly effective in creating a single market for electrical equipment and protecting safety, with no major differences in interpretation between Member States; market surveillance, especially of online sales, was the weak point. Stakeholders supplied little quantitative cost data.

indicators.objective: No monitoring indicators set in the proposal; assessed through the Commission's reports listed below

literature.citation: European Commission (2021), Evaluation of the Low Voltage Directive 2014/35/EU, SWD(2021) 202
literature.title: Evaluation of the Low Voltage Directive 2014/35/EU
literature.headline: Fairly effective for the internal market and health and safety; harmonised standards keep it up to date; market surveillance, notably of e-commerce, ineffective; benefits judged to outweigh costs but little quantitative data
literature.summary_plain: The Commission found the safety rules for electrical equipment work, but that unsafe products sold online often slip through.
literature.quality: Commission self-assessment based on stakeholder views
